findings.title: WinRAR 7.13 Final released
findings.summary_md: RARLAB's release notes for WinRAR 7.13, dated July 30, 2025, list CVE-2025-8088 as a critical directory traversal vulnerability in the Windows versions of WinRAR, RAR, UnRAR, UnRAR.dll, and portable UnRAR, letting crafted archives bypass the user-specified extraction path and write to unintended locations. Linux/Unix builds and RAR for Android are not affected. RARLAB credits Anton Cherepanov, Peter Kosinar, and Peter Strycek of ESET for the report; the page notes the release notes were updated on August 12, 2025.

findings.title: CVE-2025-8088
findings.summary_md: NVD published CVE-2025-8088 on August 8, 2025: a path traversal vulnerability in the Windows version of WinRAR that allows arbitrary code execution via maliciously crafted archive files. The record marks the vulnerability as exploited in the wild and credits discovery to Anton Cherepanov, Peter Kosinar, and Peter Strycek of ESET.

findings.title: Update WinRAR tools now: RomCom and others exploiting zero-day vulnerability
findings.summary_md: ESET researchers Anton Cherepanov, Peter Strycek, and Damien Schaeffer disclosed that CVE-2025-8088, a zero-day path traversal in WinRAR that abuses alternate data streams, was exploited in the wild starting July 18, 2025. WinRAR 7.13 beta 1 shipped July 24, 2025 and final 7.13 on July 30, 2025. Russia-aligned RomCom delivered SnipBot, RustyClaw, and Mythic agent backdoors through CV-themed RAR lures aimed at financial, manufacturing, defense, and logistics organizations in Europe and Canada between July 18 and 21, 2025, and ESET noted a second exploiting actor whose research was independently published by BI.ZONE.

findings.title: RARLAB WinRAR Path Traversal Vulnerability (CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog)
findings.summary_md: CISA added CVE-2025-8088 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on August 12, 2025 with a federal remediation due date of September 2, 2025. The entry describes a path traversal in the Windows version of WinRAR allowing arbitrary code execution via crafted archives and flags known ransomware campaign use.

findings.title: High-severity WinRAR 0-day exploited for weeks by 2 groups
findings.summary_md: Ars Technica reported that the high-severity WinRAR zero-day had been exploited for weeks by two distinct groups. The piece noted the exploits allow persistent backdooring when targets open a booby-trapped archive.

findings.title: FSB's matryoshka #1/3 - Gamaredon's gifts that keeps unpacking - GammaPhish and GammaWorm
findings.summary_md: Sekoia's TDR team published part one of its FSB Matryoshka series on June 1, 2026, reconstructing a January 2026 Gamaredon infection chain that begins with weaponized XHTML smuggling a RAR exploiting CVE-2025-8088 to drop an HTA into the Windows Startup folder. GammaWorm, a VBScript worm exceeding 20,000 obfuscated lines, hides modules in NTFS Alternate Data Streams and resolves C2 through Telegram, Telegra.ph, Teletype.in, and Cloudflare Workers dead drops. The article also cites Google Threat Intelligence Group reporting exploitation of the same vulnerability by Sandworm, Turla, Gamaredon, and China-nexus intrusion sets.
